paper_metadata.title: Microstructure informatics: Using computer vision for the characterization of dendrite growth phenomena in Ni-base single crystal Superalloys

evidence.quote: competitive dendrite growth during directional solidification of single crystal Ni-base superalloys (SXs)
three experimental steps were taken working with a CMSX-4 type of alloy
The data collected in the present work were collected from a cylindrical bar of a single crystal superalloy of type CMSX-4, which was directionally solidified using a seeded Bridgman technique

which was directionally solidified using a seeded Bridgman technique [15]. All microstructural details of the CMSX-4 seed crystal were determined [54]. The targeted [001] solidification direction was imposed parallel to the longitudinal z-direction of the cylindrical bar.

The cylindrical SX-bar of a diameter of 12 mm and a length of 120 mm was obtained as described in [15], Fig. 1. Fig. 1a shows the dimensions of the cylindrical bar. Fig. 1b defines a xS,yS,zS-coordinate system, schematically illustrates a few dendrites in wire frame mode (black lines in cylinder)

Crystal mosaicity refers to small orientation differences which exist within a real single crystal [5]. In SXs mosaicity is related to the growth and deformation of dendrites during solidification [15–19]. These slightly misoriented regions are separated by low angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) which are associated with dislocation networks [17,20].

evidence.quote: The performance of different deep learning classification architectures (AlexNet, GoogleNet and MobileNetV2) in combination with a YOLOv2 subdetection network is investigated. The network hyper parameters were optimized to achieve detection rates > 99 %.
